title: Long, Tall and Heavy
short: Describe things by length, height or weight.

blocks.html: Things can be measured. We can ask: How long is it? How tall is it? How heavy is it?

blocks.name: k-pic
blocks.cap: The tree is tall. The flower is short.

blocks.name: k-pic
blocks.cap: The watermelon is heavy, so its side goes down. The feather is light.

items: Long or short: how far it goes from end to end.
Heavy or light: how hard it is to lift.

blocks.html: Length, height and weight are things we can measure. Color and name are not.
Measuring tells “how much.” A thing can have more or less length or weight, but it cannot have more or less “red.”

blocks.title: A backpack
blocks.q: What can you measure about a backpack?
steps: Lift it: how heavy is it?
Look from bottom to top: how tall is it?
Both of these can be measured.
blocks.a: How heavy it is and how tall it is

blocks.html: For grown-ups: Use the words long, short, tall, heavy and light in everyday talk: “This bag is heavy. This ribbon is long.”

sources.name: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics, Kindergarten, K.MD.A.1: describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight
